para.text: Data inside a single element are obtained by linear interpolation of the data at the relevant corners of the element (either two, four or eight).

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: The finest resolution is obtained by pixel-by-pixel operations. This is slow but not necessarily slower than a presentation in polygons, as the plotting of a polygon requires a large amount of overhead. The time for polygon plots is mainly determined by the number of polygons, not by their size, while the time for pixel-by-pixel plots is mainly determined by the total number of pixels and thus by the size of the image.

para.text: Note however that pixel-by-pixel operations are only available on-screen, and not in Metafiles or high-res plotting. For the latter the style will automatically be changed into a style that uses polygons (with lower resolution).
